idiom_name: test-support translation unit: per-struct default factory plus override helpers
implementation_notes: C has neither classes nor default arguments, so the builder is hand-written: a test-support translation unit exposes a per-struct factory such as 'struct user user_default(void)' that returns a fully populated valid instance, and a test copies it and overwrites the single field it asserts on (or calls helpers like user_set_email(&u, "bad@example.com") that keep the override step out of the test body). C99 designated initializers make one struct literal self-documenting and can serve as the override step for flat structs, but they cannot supply the safe defaults, because members not named in the initializer are zero-initialized - so the defaults must still come from the factory. Hand-write a chainable builder (a struct user_builder plus ub_with_* functions) only for large graphs that many tests assemble step by step; the factory-and-assignment form stays the idiomatic one.
pitfalls: Defaults that hand out pointers or embedded buffers are shared between calls; allocate and fill owned memory per call, or the first test that mutates a field changes the default for every later test.
Ownership is implicit: helpers that fill an out-parameter can truncate, leak or leave the caller guessing who frees the strings; return small structs by value and document the lifetime of the rest.
A newly required field only shows up as a compile error where the factory and the tests are recompiled; keep every default in the one factory so the repair is a single edit rather than one per test.
